request: Replace the commit leg of the memory staleness predicate with a witness on the entry governs: paths, falling back to the 30-day last-touched leg when governs is absent. Collapse the duplicated STALE_COMMITS/STALE_DAYS constants into one shared module. Decay exemptions unchanged.
novelty_evidence: Derives from the recorded convention `a-rule-shared-by-a-guard-and-its-preflight-lives-in-one-module` (.claude/memory/conventions/), which names this exact smell and its rationale. Measured on disk 2026-08-23: 132 commits in 30 days makes STALE_COMMITS=30 expire an entry after 4 days; 259 of 291 non-exempt entries read stale while only 33 entries repo-wide are 30+ days old. Witnessing governs: against verified-at splits the non-exempt set 63 stale / 44 fresh / 184 recent-and-unwitnessable / 0 old-and-unwitnessable. The constant is duplicated at sweep.mjs:65-66 and hooks/lib/memory_session_start.mjs:28-29, with tests/sweep-staleness-parity.test.mjs existing because the two already drifted once (287 vs 248 at 1b2b0c7).
track_reason: Heavier than chore because the predicate is code with measurable failing cases; lighter than spec-entry because the design is settled, the failing cases are already measured, and gate A would re-ask a direction the human just chose. Security runs regardless — the write set intersects .claude/hooks/lib/**.

decisions.point: Where does the shared predicate live?
decisions.chosen: A new stdlib-only module .claude/hooks/lib/staleness.mjs that both callers import; each caller keeps its own parsing and git call and passes the results in.
decisions.rationale: The recorded convention names two worked examples, hooks/lib/design-calls.mjs and hooks/lib/write-set-profile.mjs, and both put the shared rule in hooks/lib. It also keeps the reuse of matchesAnyGlob from the sibling hooks/lib/glob-match.mjs a local import.

decisions.point: What happens to an entry with no governs: list?
decisions.chosen: Fall back to the 30-day last-touched leg, unchanged.
decisions.rationale: 184 of 291 non-exempt entries carry no governs:, and none of them is 30+ days old, so the fallback flags zero entries today. Dropping them from decay entirely would be a silent coverage loss.

decisions.chosen: No. backlog stays STALE_EXEMPT and decisions stays SUPERSESSION_DRIVEN.
decisions.rationale: Widening or narrowing the exempt classes is a separate decision with its own rationale recorded in categories.mjs. Art. VI.4 — not this workflows scope.

decisions.point: Route the witness through the derived by_path index instead of matching globs?
decisions.chosen: No. Match the governs globs directly in the pure predicate.
decisions.rationale: governed-memory.mjs warns against a reader re-scanning categories and matching globs itself, because that left the derived index unreachable. That defect was about answering `which entries govern path P` for surfacing, which the index does own. This predicate asks the different question `did entry E surface move since ITS verified-at`, which needs a per-entry changed set the index has no notion of. Keeping the predicate pure also keeps it testable without git.
